props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who slaughtered its two offspring and then slaughtered it incurs the forty
the Merciful One said 'it and its offspring', not 'its offspring and it'
the baraita: from 'it and its offspring' I have only it-then-its-offspring; whence it-then-its-mother? when it says 'you (pl.) shall not slaughter' -- here are two
one slaughters the cow, one slaughters its mother, and one slaughters its offspring -- the latter two are liable
the Merciful One wrote 'lo tishchatu': [the prohibition holds] even for two [slaughterers]
what is 'lo tishchatu'? conclude two things from it

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: כשהוא אומר לא תשחטו -- הרי כאן שנים... שנים האחרונים חייבין

deflected_by.gloss_en: האי מיבעי ליה לגופיה? -- the verse is needed for the prohibition itself and cannot also yield it-then-its-mother

refuted_by.gloss_en: אם כן ליכתוב לא תשחוט, מאי לא תשחטו? -- for the prohibition alone the singular would do; the plural is extra

deflected_by.gloss_en: ואכתי מיבעי ליה: דאי כתב רחמנא לא תשחוט הוה אמינא חד -- אין, תרי -- לא; כתב רחמנא לא תשחטו, ואפילו תרי -- the plural is still needed, to include two slaughterers

refuted_by.gloss_en: אם כן לכתוב לא ישחטו! מאי לא תשחטו? שמע מינה תרתי -- 'they shall not be slaughtered' would have covered two slaughterers; the second-person plural teaches both

objections.gloss_en: אמאי? אותו ואת בנו אמר רחמנא ולא בנו ואותו -- why should one who slaughters the offspring first and then the mother be liable?

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דתניא -- the baraita derives it-then-its-mother from the plural לא תשחטו
